qg1.intro: The Orthodox Queen's Gambit Declined. White pins with the dark-squared bishop, builds the centre, and meets the capture on c4 with the bishop and the knight trade on d5.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and declines the gambit. The dark-squared bishop gets out, and the light-squared bishop stays in for now.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8. The pin is the start of the Orthodox.
Be7 breaks that pin by stepping the dark-squared bishop between the knight and the queen, and prepares castling.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop. The dark-squared bishop is already outside the chain.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares castling. It also watches the centre.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the knight on f6. Black keeps the c-pawn free.
Rc1 puts the rook behind the pawn on c4. Both c-pawns are still on the board.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and keeps the centre solid. The rook on c1 is staring at this pawn.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims at the kingside. Black usually takes on c4 now, so the bishop will move twice.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and releases the centre. The light-squared bishop has to move again.
Bxc4 recaptures the pawn on c4. The bishop spent a move, and Black uses that tempo.
Nd5 plants the knight in the centre and attacks the knight on c3. The trade of dark-squared bishops is the classical idea.
Bxe7 takes the bishop on e7. White accepts the trade the knight asked for.
Qxe7 recaptures the bishop on e7. The queen is developed, and the dark-squared bishops are gone.

qg2.intro: The Queen's Gambit Accepted. White takes the pawn back with the light-squared bishop, castles, and tucks that bishop to b3.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and accepts the gambit. Black will give the pawn back and fight with piece play.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and stops the pawn on c4 being held too easily. It also watches the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and prepares to challenge the centre.
e3 prepares to take the pawn back and frees the light-squared bishop. It also supports the pawn on d4.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop and builds a solid shell. The light-squared bishop will come out later.
Bxc4 takes the pawn on c4. The gambit pawn comes home, and the bishop is developed.
c5 hits the pawn on d4. This is how Black fights the centre once the pawn has been returned.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
a6 takes b5 away from White and prepares queenside expansion.
Bb3 drops the bishop back before a queenside pawn can hit it, and keeps the diagonal from a2.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.

qg3.intro: The Czech Slav. a4 stops the queenside expansion, White takes the pawn back, and e4 gains space against the bishop on g6.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the light-squared bishop free. That is the Slav.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and controls the centre before the queen's knight comes out.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the centre.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4. Black will try to hold it with a queenside pawn, which White now stops.
a4 stops that queenside pawn and gains space. The pawn on c4 will be taken back by the bishop.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the chain. This is why the c-pawn moved instead of the e-pawn.
e3 prepares to take the pawn back and frees the light-squared bishop. It supports the pawn on d4.
e6 supports the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop. The light-squared bishop is already on f5.
Bxc4 takes the pawn on c4. The gambit pawn comes home to an active diagonal.
Bb4 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on c3. Black uses the pin to finish development.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king leaves before the centre opens.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Qe2 develops the queen and supports the coming central push.
Bg6 keeps the light-squared bishop and steps off the diagonal the e-pawn wants.
e4 gains space and builds a full pawn centre. The bishop on g6 is now staring at that pawn.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. Black castles into White's pawn centre.

qg4.intro: The Meran Semi-Slav. Black takes on c4, expands with b5, and White strikes in the centre with e4.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
c6 supports the pawn on d5. The light-squared bishop is not yet shut in, but Black will also play the e-pawn.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and controls the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop. Together with the c-pawn, this is the Semi-Slav.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop. White is ready to take the pawn back if it is captured.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports a capture on c4. The king's knight stays on f6.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims at the kingside. If Black takes on c4, this bishop takes back.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4. The Meran starts with this capture and a queenside advance.
Bxc4 recaptures the pawn on c4. The bishop will be asked to move again by the b-pawn.
b5 attacks the bishop on c4 and gains queenside space. This tempo is the point of the capture.
Bd3 drops the light-squared bishop back and keeps it aimed at the kingside. White does not trade it for a pawn.
Bb7 develops the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal, aiming at the centre.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
a6 supports the pawn on b5 and prepares the central hit.
e4 gains space and strikes in the centre before Black's hit arrives.
c5 hits the pawn on d4 and challenges the new centre. This is the Meran break.

qg5.intro: The Chigorin. Black develops the queen's knight and the light-squared bishop, and White accepts doubled pawns for the centre and the bishop pair.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4. The Chigorin uses a piece instead of a pawn to meet the gambit.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Bg4 attacks the knight on f3. The pawn on e2 still stands behind that knight, so this is pressure on the knight rather than a pin to the queen.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and opens the centre. Black is invited to take the knight.
Bxf3 takes the knight on f3. Black gives up the light-squared bishop to damage White's pawns.
gxf3 recaptures the bishop on f3. White accepts doubled pawns and keeps the centre.
Qxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and develops the queen into the centre.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop. The king's knight is gone, so this pawn has to hold the centre.
e5 challenges the pawn on d4 and opens a diagonal for the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the queen on d5.
Bb4 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on c3. The queen has a moment because the knight is busy.
Bd2 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on c3.
Bxc3 takes the knight on c3. Black trades the dark-squared bishop as well.
bxc3 recaptures the bishop on c3. White's queenside pawns are split, but the centre stays full.
exd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the e-file.
cxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4 and restores a pawn in the centre.
Nge7 develops the king's knight toward the centre.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal. The fianchetto makes sense of the doubled kingside pawns.
Qe6 steps the queen to a stable square and keeps an eye on the centre.

qg6.intro: The Tartakower. Black asks the dark-squared bishop a question, fianchettoes the other bishop's pawn, and the knights come off on d5.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and declines the gambit. The dark-squared bishop gets out, and the light-squared bishop stays in for now.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8. The pin is the start of the Orthodox.
Be7 breaks that pin by stepping the dark-squared bishop between the knight and the queen, and prepares castling.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop. The dark-squared bishop is already outside the chain.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares castling. It also watches the centre.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question now that the king is castled. The bishop should not sit there against the knight on f6.
Bh4 keeps the dark-squared bishop and maintains the pressure on the knight on f6.
b6 prepares a fianchetto. The light-squared bishop needs a diagonal, because the e-pawn has shut its old one.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and opens the centre before that bishop arrives.
Nxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and plants a knight where it can be traded.
Bxe7 takes the bishop on e7. The dark-squared bishops come off, and the queen will recapture.
Qxe7 recaptures the bishop on e7. The queen is developed.
Nxd5 takes the knight on d5. White removes the blockading knight.
exd5 recaptures the knight on d5. The pawn on c7 still stands beside the pawn on d5.
Rc1 puts the rook on the half-open c-file. The pawn on d5 still has its neighbour on the c-file.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop and defends the pawn on d5. The bishop has found its square.

qg7.intro: The Tarrasch. Black hits back with c5, the centre opens, and White fianchettos against the pawn on d5.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and declines the gambit. The dark-squared bishop gets out, and the light-squared bishop stays in for now.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
c5 hits back at the pawn on d4. The Tarrasch fights the centre with a pawn.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and opens the centre. The pawn on c5 is still beside the d-file.
exd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and opens the e-file. The pawn on d5 will be the long-term target.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares the fianchetto. The pawn on d5 is the centre Black has accepted.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
g3 prepares a fianchetto. The light-squared bishop belongs on the long diagonal.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and supports the centre.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal. The knight on f3 still stands on that diagonal.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The bishop on g2 is already at work.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bg5 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on f6.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop and defends the pawn on d5. The bishop has found its square.

qg8.intro: The Cambridge Springs. The queen comes to a5 against the pinned knight, and the dark-squared bishop joins her on b4.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and declines the gambit. The dark-squared bishop gets out, and the light-squared bishop stays in for now.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8. The pin is the start of the Orthodox.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6, so the pin does not cost the knight. This is the Cambridge Springs.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop. The dark-squared bishop is already outside the chain.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the queen a path toward the queenside.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. The queen is about to pin the other knight.
Qa5 attacks along the diagonal toward the knight on c3. The queen and the coming bishop are the idea.
Nd2 puts a second piece on the a5-e1 diagonal, so the knight on c3 is no longer pinned to the king.
Bb4 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on c3. The queen on a5 and this bishop are Black's active pieces.
Qc2 develops the queen and adds a defender to the knight on c3. She also watches the centre.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. Black castles with the queenside pressure already built.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and prepares castling. White finishes calmly against the pin.

qg9.intro: The Albin Counter-Gambit. Black plants a pawn on d4, and White fianchettos against it, castles, and trades the knights.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
e5 offers a pawn to plant one on d4. This is the Albin, not a quiet decline.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and accepts the gambit.
d4 plants the pawn in the centre. That wedge was the point of the offer.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
g3 prepares a fianchetto against the pawn on d4. The long diagonal is how White handles the wedge.
Nge7 develops the king's knight toward g6, where it can help recover the pawn.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal, aiming at the queenside once the knight on f3 moves.
Ng6 eyes the pawn on e5. Black wants the gambit pawn back.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king is safe behind the fianchetto.
Ngxe5 takes the pawn on e5. The gambit pawn comes back, and the knight on f3 can trade.
Nxe5 takes the knight on e5 and trades a pair of knights.
Nxe5 recaptures the knight on e5. The knights come off, and the pawn on d4 remains the feature.
Na3 develops the queen's knight toward b5, where it can annoy the pawn on d4.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.

qg10.intro: The Moscow. White takes the knight on f6, the queen recaptures, and Black prepares a fianchetto after taking on c4.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre. Black is ready to decline or take the gambit pawn.
c4 attacks the pawn on d5. White offers a wing pawn: taking it draws the centre pawn off d5, and declining leaves the pressure on.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the light-squared bishop free. That is the Slav.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and controls the centre before the queen's knight comes out.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the centre.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
e6 supports the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop. The light-squared bishop stays in, which this line accepts.
Bg5 attacks the knight on f6 and offers the trade that defines the Moscow.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question before Black commits the king.
Bxf6 takes the knight on f6. White gives up the dark-squared bishop to spoil Black's development.
Qxf6 recaptures the bishop on f6. The queen comes out early, which is the price of the trade.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop.
Nd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre. The king's knight has already been traded.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims at the kingside.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4. Black releases the centre now that the queen is out.
Bxc4 recaptures the pawn on c4. The bishop moves twice, and Black uses the tempo for a fianchetto.
g6 prepares the dark-squared bishop's fianchetto. The queen on f6 already sits beside that diagonal.
